assessment.support_scope: Partial financial support for this study was provided by a grant from the EuroQol Reasearch Foundation, EQ Project 1487-RA.
assessment.reason: Two related experiments directly examined whether TTO and EQ-VAS tasks evoke unconscious death-thought accessibility and whether death-thought accessibility and attachment affect TTO and EQ-VAS scores. The EuroQol Research Foundation provided partial financial support.

studies.label: Study 1: online experiment with an unconscious cultural-worldview-defense measure

items.statement: The pooled findings indicate that TTO and EQ-VAS tasks did not evoke elevated unconscious death-thought accessibility in the online experiments.
The authors interpret EQ-VAS sensitivity to DTA as evidence that EQ-VAS can capture a broader psychological concept than TTO.
The absence of an association between DTA and hypothetical wheelchair TTO scores suggests limited DTA impact on national health valuation studies in this online context.
Attachment appears relevant to valuation of self-experienced health but not to the hypothetical wheelchair health state.
DTA was measured after the wheelchair TTO or EQ-VAS task but before the self-experienced-health TTO or EQ-VAS task, which can affect associations.
The Study 2 conscious defense measure was not significant and was excluded from further analyses.
source: Full article, Electronic supplementary material > Appendix > Conscious defense strength > Results

items.evidence: Findings f1/f6, f2/f7, f3/f8, and f5/f12 use pooled data from Study 1 and Study 2. The schema permits only one study_id for each Finding, so each pooled finding is repeated under both studies.
items.importance: Without a multi-Study relation, a pooled finding can appear to belong to only one study.
items.proposed_resolution: Add a relation that lets one Finding link to multiple Study records while preserving one finding identity.
